idiom_name: generator function (function* with yield) as a pull-based unfold
implementation_notes: Generator functions are JavaScript's language-level unfold: a function* that advances a seed and yields one layer per iteration compiles to a suspended state machine with pull semantics, so no combinator is needed and callers pull with next() or for...of. Generators are lazy but single-use and unmemoised, so a second traversal needs a new generator; Array.from or spread forces the whole structure, and library forms such as Ramda's R.unfold deliberately materialise an array until the step function returns false. Tree-shaped unfolds remain hand-written recursion or explicit-stack traversal, because the generator protocol linearises one sequence at a time.
pitfalls: A generator object is one-shot: after for...of exhausts it, further iteration yields nothing, so shared sequences must be re-created or cached.
Spreading an unbounded generator ([...gen], Array.from(gen)) hangs or exhausts memory; bound it with a take/limit helper before materialising.
yield does not pause across a callback or a promise boundary: asynchronous generation needs async function* and for await.
